newsitem.title: UK: EMI gains, extending bounce from 2-yr low.
newsitem.headline: EMI gains, extending bounce from 2-yr low.

text.p: Shares in EMI Group Plc rose in thin trading on Tuesday as their recent decline to a near two-year low of 10.80 stg continued to lure some investors into the music publisher, dealers said.
"There must be a buyer in the market and it is not a particularly liquid stock," said a market-maker at one top brokerage.
The stock was up 25p or 2.2 percent at 11.80 stg by 1057 GMT in thin volume of 176,127 shares.

EMI shares have been under pressure for much of this year amid fears of growing price competition among music retailers. In February, it reported a six percent decline in pre-tax profit for the nine months through December.
However, EMI bounced early this month as NatWest Securities tipped the stock as a good long-term play.
EMI unit Virgin Records said last week the Spice Girls had sold over 10 million copies of the debut album -- putting them among the top-selling British artists of all time.
The group, currently in the U.S., will make their live debut at a concert in Manchester in May.
